$comment: Isoloop and the alternatives, for the home page's table and the Compared tab on /features/ (docs/plans/0.1.1-site.md, decision 11). Every cell is sourced from that project's own docs, with the date it was checked. Validated by build/alternatives.ts. Marks: yes, partial or no. No benchmarks against the alternatives.

ui.note: Each isolate renders in a worker, and the page applies its DOM changes. Layout reads and focus are asynchronous.

supervision.note: Heartbeats, restarts with backoff, a fallback after repeated crashes, and catch-up from the bus.

bus.note: Topics with retention, replay and consumer groups, and an optional copy on disk.

security.note: It contains crashes and hangs from code you trust. Isolates run on the page's origin, so hostile code belongs in a cross-origin iframe.

browsers.note: Chrome 108, Firefox 114 and Safari 16.4 or later.

cost.note: More CPU across threads, more memory and a slower start than native code with workers. The main thread still applies every DOM change.

rows.name: Remote DOM
rows.betterFor: Rendering untrusted extension UI from a set of elements the host defines, with the remote code in a sandboxed iframe.

ui.note: Renders from a hidden iframe or, with its DOM polyfill, from a worker. The host page mirrors the elements.

supervision.note: Its docs describe no restart for a remote side that crashes or hangs.

bus.note: It sends DOM changes from the remote side to the host. There's no log to replay.

security.note: The boundary is the sandbox you run the remote side in. The host can limit which elements it creates.

browsers.note: Not stated. The remote side needs custom elements and MutationObserver, or the DOM polyfill in a worker.

cost.note: You build the host, the sandbox and the channel between them, and decide which elements the remote side may render.

rows.name: Partytown
rows.betterFor: Moving third-party scripts such as tag managers and analytics off the main thread without changing them.

ui.note: Runs third-party scripts in a worker against a proxied DOM. Its docs say scripts that build UI aren't a good fit.

supervision.note: Its docs describe no restart for a script that crashes or hangs.

bus.note: Scripts reach the page through a proxy. There's no log to replay.

security.note: You can allow or deny each script access to main-thread APIs, cookies and storage.

browsers.note: Every browser. Without service workers or Atomics, scripts run on the main thread as before.

cost.note: Each DOM call from the worker is a blocking round trip, throttled on purpose, and `preventDefault()` has no effect. It needs a service worker, or extra response headers for Atomics.

ui.note: A DOM in a worker, which sends its changes to the main thread.

supervision.note: Its docs describe no restart for a worker that crashes or hangs.

bus.note: It sends DOM changes to the main thread. There's no log to replay.

security.note: Its AMP build adds hooks for safety features such as HTML sanitization.

browsers.note: The latest two versions of the major browsers, on desktop and mobile.

cost.note: Its docs call it an in-progress DOM: `querySelector` works in part, and APIs such as History aren't there yet.

rows.name: Comlink + workers
rows.betterFor: Moving computation, not UI, off the main thread with a 1.1 kB library.

ui.note: Workers have no DOM. Comlink turns calls to a worker into promises.

supervision.note: Errors are thrown again on the calling side. Nothing restarts a worker.

bus.note: Remote calls over `postMessage`. There's no log to replay.

security.note: It adds no boundary of its own.

browsers.note: Chrome 56, Firefox 52 and Safari 10.1 or later.

cost.note: Every call is asynchronous, and you split the app between the page and its workers yourself.

rows.name: Cross-origin iframes
rows.betterFor: Code you don't trust at all: the browser keeps another origin out of the page.

ui.note: A frame is a separate document, not a worker.

supervision.note: Nothing restarts a frame that crashes or hangs.

bus.note: The page and its frames talk through `postMessage`. There's no log to replay.

security.note: The same-origin policy keeps the frame out of the page's DOM, cookies and storage, and `sandbox` restricts it further.

cost.note: Each frame is a complete document with its own memory and compute, and it shares nothing with the page but messages.

rows.name: `scheduler.yield()`
rows.betterFor: Long tasks that must stay on the main thread and can be split, without workers or a new architecture.

ui.note: Work stays on the main thread, which it hands back between pieces.

supervision.note: A browser API for scheduling, with nothing to restart.

bus.note: It schedules work and carries no messages.

browsers.note: Chrome and Edge 129 and Firefox 142 or later. Not in Safari.

cost.note: You split each long task by hand, and the main thread still runs all of it.
